Label Trustworthiness and Continuity

Source: R/label-trustworthiness-continuity.R
label_trustworthiness_continuity.Rd

For each pair of classes, what fraction of observations lie closer to their own class centroid? Compare that fraction in the reference and the embedding to see which classes have become harder or easier to tell apart.

Usage

label_trustworthiness_continuity(Xin, Xout, labels, ret_extra = FALSE)

Arguments

Xin

Reference coordinates, as a dense numeric matrix or data frame with observations in rows.

Xout

Embedding coordinates for the same observations in the same order. Nonnumeric data-frame columns are ignored in both inputs.

labels

A vector without missing values, with one label per row and at least two distinct labels.

ret_extra

Whether to return the class-pair consistency scores and their signed changes.

Value

A named numeric vector with trustworthiness and continuity. With ret_extra = TRUE, a list containing scores and pairs. The data frame pairs has columns label_a, label_b, consistency_in, consistency_out, and change (output minus input). Pairs follow the first appearance of the labels.

Details

For each pair of labels and in each space, compute the two class centroids. Distance consistency is the fraction of observations nearer their own centroid in Euclidean distance. A tie counts as half a correct assignment. This implementation uses the unrescaled fraction in [0, 1] and weights observations equally within each pair. Centroids are estimated on the observations being evaluated.

Label trustworthiness is one minus the mean decrease in consistency, counting gains as zero. Label continuity is one minus the mean increase, counting losses as zero. Each unordered pair has equal weight in these means. A pair can gain consistency when the embedding exaggerates the separation visible in the reference.

Distance consistency uses one centroid per class. Compare it with roc_auc() or pr_auc() when classes have multiple clusters or irregular shapes. Nonfinite computed centroid distances cause an error.

Scaling

This is a full-data option when the number of classes is modest. Each row is compared with its own centroid and each other class centroid. With C classes the summaries cover C * (C - 1) / 2 pairs. No observation-level distance matrix is required.

References

Jeon, H., Kuo, Y.-H., Aupetit, M., Ma, K.-L., & Seo, J. (2024). Classes are not Clusters: Improving Label-based Evaluation of Dimensionality Reduction. doi:10.1109/TVCG.2023.3327187 Their ltnc package compares classes in pairs. Quadra uses the fraction closer to their own centroid for each pair, following the distance consistency criterion of Sips, Neubert, Lewis and Hanrahan (2009). doi:10.1111/j.1467-8659.2009.01467.x

See also

roc_auc(), pr_auc()

Examples

x <- as.matrix(iris[, -5])
y <- prcomp(x, rank. = 2)$x
label_trustworthiness_continuity(x, y, iris$Species, ret_extra = TRUE)
#> $scores
#> trustworthiness      continuity 
#>               1               1 
#> 
#> $pairs
#>      label_a    label_b consistency_in consistency_out change
#> 1     setosa versicolor           1.00            1.00      0
#> 2     setosa  virginica           1.00            1.00      0
#> 3 versicolor  virginica           0.89            0.89      0
#>
